title: Full Stack Developer
card_description: Pre-filled with optimized power words for both frontend and backend engineering, matching top ATS requirements.
description: By: David - Director of Engineering | Hey, I'm David. I look at about fifty junior developer resumes a week. Honestly? Most of them go straight in the bin. Why? Because people just list out 15 different frameworks without telling me how they actually connect together. I built this template to fix that.
core_philosophy: My philosophy is simple: show me the architecture. Don't give me a shopping list of tools. I want you to use this layout to explain exactly how you separated your frontend View from your backend Controller. If you can't explain your state management, I can't put you on a real project.
personal_story: When I was trying to get my first junior role, I got rejected 7 times in a row. My resume just listed 'React' and 'Node.js'. Finally, a mentor told me to change my approach. For my next application, I explicitly wrote out how my e-commerce project's API was too slow, and exactly how I implemented Redis to fix the load times. The recruiter called me the next morning. They don't want to see what you built; they want to see the problems you hit and how you handled them. Do exactly that in your project section.
ats_optimizations: I made sure this template forces you to use the exact keywords my HR software scans for, like JSON Web Tokens and RESTful APIs.
I put the Academic Projects section at the very top. This is a neat trick I learned to hide the fact that you don't have professional experience yet.
I formatted the GitHub links so that my recruiter's automated scraper grabs your portfolio data instantly.
I changed all the phrasing. Instead of saying 'Developed an app', this template makes you say 'Architected a full-stack CRUD application', because that's how we talk on the job.

title: Data Analyst
card_description: Packed with actionable verbs and data translation keywords designed strictly to bypass initial automated screenings.
description: By: Priya - Lead Data Analyst | Hi, I'm Priya. When I interview junior analysts, I usually don't care if they know how to open Tableau. What I care about is whether their data can stop our company from losing money. I designed this template to stop you from acting like a human calculator.
core_philosophy: My biggest pet peeve is when people list 'SQL' as a skill without any context. This format forces you to tie your SQL queries directly to a business outcome. If your college project doesn't tell me the ROI, my HR filters are going to drop your resume before I even see it.
personal_story: I remember walking into my first real data interview. I thought they were going to quiz me on Python syntax. Instead, the hiring manager pointed to a bullet point on my resume where I mentioned 'cleaning data' and asked, 'So what?' That's when I learned the hard way. I completely rewrote my resume after that to explain how my college churn prediction project could actually help a local business identify high-risk customers before they left. You must highlight the business problem you solved, not just the tools you used.
ats_optimizations: I specifically added SQL join types (like INNER and LEFT) into the bullet points because I know our system filters out resumes without them.
I organized the tools into Visualization, Database, and Scripting sections so the robotic parsers don't get confused.
I made sure every bullet point requires a measurable impact figure (like 'reduced time by 20%') instead of vague responsibilities.
I included A/B testing methodologies because marketing teams are begging for that skill right now, and no one puts it on their resume.

title: Data Engineer
card_description: Features optimal vocabulary for ETL pipelines, big data integration, and data warehousing to stand out to recruiter AIs.
description: By: Marcus - Principal Data Architect | Hey, Marcus here. I don't care if your dashboard looks pretty. I need to know your ETL pipeline won't fail when we push a million rows of data through it. I put this layout together to help you show that you understand deep-level infrastructure.
core_philosophy: In my world, reliability is everything. I stripped all the UI/UX fluff out of this template. It focuses entirely on your batch processing algorithms and how you move data around without breaking the system. That's how you prove to me that you aren't a liability on a Friday afternoon.
personal_story: People always ask how I landed a Senior Data Architect role so quickly. The secret is that I stopped talking about 'dashboards' on my resume and started talking about 'failures.' In my project section, I detailed a time my raw log pipeline crashed under a massive load, and the exact steps I took to orchestrate a fix using Apache Airflow. Hiring managers want to see that you've been in the trenches and survived. Put your biggest technical failure and your solution front and center.
ats_optimizations: I added cloud-native terms like Data Lakes and Serverless Computing so you can bypass the strict enterprise IT scanners.
I formatted the skills section to put Python directly next to your data frameworks, so the parsing bots link the two concepts together.
I styled the academic project section to look exactly like real-world enterprise infrastructure builds.
I completely removed non-relevant keywords to keep your keyword density 100% focused on backend data integration.

title: Software Engineer
card_description: Standardized, cleanly formatted generic engineering templates filled with algorithmic problem-solving and SDLC buzzwords.
description: By: Elena - VP of Engineering | Hi, I'm Elena. Please stop using crazy colors, progress bars, and multiple columns on your resume. It breaks our automated parsers and I never get to read it. I created this ultra-clean template because I only care about your core computer science logic.
core_philosophy: I believe a software engineer's resume should be as clean as their code. This format isolates your algorithmic problem-solving. It forces you to explain the Big O time complexity of your projects so I know you actually understand what you're doing.
personal_story: In 2018, I interviewed for an elite backend role. The only reason my resume was pulled from the stack of 500 applicants was because I didn't just say 'Built a chat app.' I dedicated three bullet points to explaining how my server had massive memory leaks when concurrent users spiked, and how I refactored the threading model to fix it. If you want to get shortlisted by me today, you need to show me the exact bottleneck you encountered and the algorithmic approach you used to resolve it.
ats_optimizations: I removed every single image and complex table to ensure a perfect parse rate on legacy systems like Workday.
I separated your programming languages from your software environments to make it easier for our initial bot scan.
I built unit testing and debugging skills natively into the academic bullet points.
I added specific phrasing around memory management to prove you have fundamental computer science competency.

title: Data Scientist
card_description: Highlight your statistical modeling, machine learning, and data visualization expertise using verified industry phrasing.
description: By: James - Staff Data Scientist | Hey folks, James here. The data science field is flooded right now with people who just run a basic linear regression script and call themselves experts. I designed this template to force you to talk about real deployment, not just textbook theory.
core_philosophy: I really don't want to just see a high accuracy metric. I want to know how you handled the missing values and how you eventually put that model into a live environment. This layout bridges the gap between your Kaggle competitions and the corporate engineering work I do every day.
personal_story: I'll never forget the advice that got me into Big Tech. My resume was full of Kaggle competitions with perfect accuracy scores. A senior scientist looked at it and laughed. He told me, 'Real world data is messy. Where is the mess here?' I went home and changed my entire resume to focus on how I handled missing, dirty data and severe model overfitting in my pricing algorithm. That is what recruiters are looking for—how you handle the chaos of real data.
ats_optimizations: I balanced the machine learning terms with basic statistical forecasting words so you satisfy both the HR scanners and my Lead Engineers.
I highlighted data preparation right next to model tuning so you look like a comprehensive full-stack data scientist.
I formatted the GitHub and Kaggle links so the ATS bots actually register them as valid portfolio artifacts.
I prioritized feature engineering over simple algorithm name-dropping to show you have deep domain knowledge.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
card_description: Targeted ATS templates packed with power words for model deployment, NLP, deep learning, and MLOps.
description: By: Alex - Head of AI Infrastructure | Alex here. Look, a model that only works on your local Jupyter notebook is completely useless to me. I need ML Engineers who can deploy to the cloud. I built this template to highlight your MLOps architecture.
core_philosophy: I shifted the focus of this resume away from raw math and heavily into endpoint structuring and Docker containerization. If you can't prove to me that you understand inferencing speed and cloud deployment, I'm simply not going to hire you.
personal_story: I used to think building the model was the hard part. My early resumes focused entirely on the math. It wasn't until I started getting ignored by recruiters that I realized the truth: companies care about deployment. I rewrote my resume to focus on the time my neural network's inference speed was too slow for a mobile app, and how I wrapped it in a Docker container to reduce latency. If you don't show the problem and your deployment solution, your resume goes in the trash.
ats_optimizations: I front-loaded the neural network architectures so you hit the high-tier specialization filters immediately.
I put your cloud platform integration skills right next to your modeling projects to satisfy our cross-disciplinary requirements.
I structured the bullet points so you have to show exact model accuracy improvements over time.
I injected specific MLOps terminology that I rarely see on junior resumes to instantly elevate your profile.

title: Business Analyst
card_description: Communicate stakeholder engagement, requirement gathering, and process optimization strictly in ATS-friendly language.
description: By: Sarah - Senior Product Manager | Hi, I'm Sarah. A Business Analyst who can't translate technical requirements into executive summaries is a massive liability for me. I designed this template to bridge the gap between your SQL queries and actual human communication.
core_philosophy: You're hired to talk to both humans and computers. This format ensures your hard technical skills are tied directly to words like 'Stakeholder Engagement'. It's highly optimized for the heavily regulated industries I work in, like banking and healthcare IT.
personal_story: The turning point in my career was when I stopped writing 'Gathered Requirements' on my resume. Everyone says that. Instead, I told a story in my project section. I explained how an accounting team was manually approving 500 invoices a month, causing huge delays, and how my AS-IS process map cut their time by 75%. You have to show the human error you encountered and the exact workflow you designed to fix it. That is how you get an interview.
ats_optimizations: I injected Agile and Scrum language throughout the document because our project management sweeps demand it.
I grouped the mapping and visualization tools together to hit the standard keyword density checks used by Fortune 500 banks.
I forced a clean, readable layout that appeals to my non-technical HR managers while keeping enough tech terms for the IT directors.
I added phrasing that highlights your cross-functional team coordination, proving you can lead without formal authority.

title: AI Engineer / GenAI
card_description: Modernized templates with prompt engineering, LLM integration, and generative AI keywords formatted for robots.
description: By: Viktor - Lead AI Researcher | Hey, Viktor here. Generative AI is a fundamentally different field, so using a standard 2020 software resume makes you look completely outdated. I built this explicitly to prove you understand prompt optimization, rather than just throwing buzzwords around.
core_philosophy: Startups hiring AI engineers right now only care about two things: RAG architectures and API cost reduction. This template isolates your Large Language Model fine-tuning skills and forces you to explain your token optimization strategies to me.
personal_story: When the LLM boom started, everyone's resume looked identical: 'Used OpenAI API.' I knew I had to stand out. So, I detailed a specific project where the standard LLM kept hallucinating answers on private company docs. I wrote out exactly how I architected a RAG pipeline to force semantic search, eliminating the hallucinations entirely. You have to prove you understand the limitations of the technology and how to engineer around them. That's what gets you hired today.
ats_optimizations: I packed this densely with the new 2026 ATS keywords dealing specifically with generative tech and latent space methodologies.
I highlighted vector databases naturally within standard software pipelines to prove your architectural competence.
I clearly separated your foundational ML knowledge from your modern generative API skills so I can verify your technological timeline.
I emphasized cost-reduction techniques in API calling, which is my number one priority when hiring.

title: Cloud Engineer
card_description: Pre-populated with essential power phrases for AWS/Azure/GCP architecture, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure as code.
description: By: Chloe - Senior Cloud Solutions Architect | Hi, Chloe here. If your resume focuses entirely on basic IT support tasks, it's going straight in the bin. I need to know you can handle highly scalable, secure infrastructure. I formatted this to highlight your continuous integration skills.
core_philosophy: I want to see your CI/CD pipelines right next to your AWS certifications. This layout walks you through framing your simple university web-hosting projects as 'High-Availability Cloud Architecture Implementations.' It forces you to highlight the exact keywords our scanners demand.
personal_story: My first big break didn't come from my AWS certifications. It came because my resume told a story about downtime. I wrote about a university project where manual server deployments caused 30 minutes of downtime, and how I used Terraform to automate a CI/CD pipeline to achieve 99% uptime. Recruiters don't want to see a list of cloud services; they want to read a story about how you automated a painful, manual problem.
ats_optimizations: I clustered the CI/CD automation tools directly next to major cloud platform names to trigger our exact-match parameters.
I built a dedicated block for cloud certifications, which are mandatory for many of the automated ATS gateways we use.
I highlighted deep Linux administration and basic bash scripting organically within the project descriptions.
I framed simple web-hosting projects as high-availability implementations to maximize your authority score.

title: Power BI Developer
card_description: Purpose-built for BI specialists who need to prove dashboard design, DAX mastery, and enterprise data modeling skills to ATS systems.
description: By: Aisha - BI Engineering Director | Aisha here. Most Power BI resumes I read are dead on arrival because they just say 'I built dashboards.' I don't need a dashboard builder; I need a full-stack BI professional. This template forces you to prove you own the entire data pipeline.
core_philosophy: I strictly look for outcome-driven language. 'Reduced reporting cycle from 5 days to 4 hours' beats 'Experienced with DAX' every single time. This layout heavily separates your Power Query from your DAX to prove to me that you understand the entire Microsoft ecosystem.
personal_story: I see a hundred resumes a week that just say 'Created visual dashboards.' It means nothing. The resume that got me my first management job didn't even mention visuals. It focused on a time when data refresh rates were taking 6 hours, and how I rewrote the underlying DAX calculations to bring it down to 15 minutes. To get shortlisted, your resume must prove you can identify performance bottlenecks and optimize the underlying data model.
ats_optimizations: I structured the skills into Data Modeling, DAX, and Visualization so our ATS parsers register your deep BI specialization.
I injected Power Platform ecosystem keywords because they are increasingly mandatory for my enterprise Microsoft environment roles.
I formatted the project descriptions to highlight Row-Level Security, an advanced keyword I rarely find on junior BI resumes.
I included explicit mention of data source connectors to satisfy both our cloud-native and on-premise job filters.
